notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR7: the debugging section 'is not executed for a specific operand more than once as a result of the execution of a single statement', a PERFORM runs it 'once for each iteration', and each imperative verb inside an imperative statement is a separate statement. StatementBinder.BindStatement, the funnel every statement (nested ones included) passes, asks DebugTriggerPlanner.Plan of the statement itself (BoundReferences never enters a nested statement) and OncePerOperand keeps one fire per target; a procedure subject fires at each entry of the paragraph (DispatchEmitter.EmitDispatchMethod), so each PERFORM iteration runs it. Probed at 85: MOVE 1 TO E(1) E(2) E(3) on an ODO table, ADD E(1) E(2) TO E(3) and ADD 1 TO I I each fire once; MOVE 2 TO I E(I) gives DEBUG-SUB-1 +0002; ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR MOVE 0 TO G1 MOVE 1 TO G1 fires G1 twice then E once; PERFORM P2 VARYING 2 iterations fires twice, 0 TIMES never; PERFORM UNTIL fires per evaluation; MOVE G TO G (group) does not fire the G1 target; a failed OPEN and a READ on an unopened file fire the file-name section after the USE procedure, the unexecuted INTO operand does not; at 2002/2023 USE FOR DEBUGGING is refused COBOL0902. The witness checks the two-operand ADD, the two MOVEs of one IF and PERFORM 3 TIMES.

next.reason: 1985: "The associated debugging section is not executed for a specific operand more than once as a result of the execution of a single statement"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Debug module; the USE statement rules (14.9.49) cover only exception and BEFORE REPORTING procedures". No 2023 clause holds USE FOR DEBUGGING. The USE candidates cover only exception and report declaratives, so 2023 drops debugging sections and this execution-count rule.
